title: `try_*` functions give NULL for their own errors only
verdict: `try_cast`, `try_add`, `try_divide`, `try_sum`, … : NULL on their errors, in both modes
description: `try_cast`, `try_add`, `try_subtract`, `try_multiply`, `try_divide`, `try_mod`, `try_sum`, `try_avg`, `try_element_at`, `try_to_number`, `try_to_timestamp` and `try_to_date` return NULL where their raising form raises (overflow, a zero divisor, malformed text, an index out of range), whatever `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` says. `try_avg` of `BIGINT` sums in double and never overflows. Two exceptions raise anyway: `try_element_at(a, 0)` raises `INVALID_INDEX_OF_ZERO` in both modes, as `element_at` does, and `try_to_timestamp` with a pattern Spark 3.0 changed raises `INCONSISTENT_BEHAVIOR_CROSS_VERSION.DATETIME_PATTERN_RECOGNITION` (a `SparkUpgradeException`).

They cover only their own operation: `try_cast(regexp_extract('a', '(', 0) AS INT)` still raises the pattern's error, and `try_divide(1, 0) + (1 div 0)` still raises under ANSI from the `div`. There is no `TRY(expr)` that covers a whole expression in SQL.
reference: Substrait's cast has `failure_behavior: RETURN_NULL`; the reference honours it on DuckDB only, and other engines refuse it until #271. `try_cast` is Spark's `RETURN_NULL`.

evidence.note: Useful Functions for ANSI Mode: the `try_*` functions

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.

evidence.note: `TRY_CAST('abc' AS int)` is NULL, ANSI on
`try_sum` of 9223372036854775807 and 1 is NULL, ANSI on
`try_avg` of 9223372036854775807 and 1 is about 4.61E18, a `double`: no overflow
`try_add(1, (2147483647 + 1))` raises `ARITHMETIC_OVERFLOW` from the inner `+`, ANSI on

provenance.notes: Spark's SQL query tests at tag v4.3.0: the golden files under results/ run with ANSI on, those under results/nonansi/ with it off.

notes: `python -m sverify_dev.spark_fuzz --rows 300 --seed 738`: random rows leaning on the fact's edges, each construct run with spark.sql.ansi.enabled on and off, on the folded and the codegen path, and compared with a model of this fact (value, result type, error class). 7200 of 7200 results as the fact says.
try_variants[0]: 300 rows, `try_add(a, b)`, `try_subtract(a, b)`, `try_multiply(a, b)`, `try_mod(a, b)`, `try_divide(a, b)`, `try_cast(s AS INT)`, 7200 of 7200 results as the fact says.
Spark 4.3.0, Java 21.0.12.1, Linux amd64, local[2], session time zone UTC.
